info.name: p3dx gov_layer - Job approval + contract signing flow
info.description:
Runs in this order:
1. Set the policy for the dataset (already in the DX catalogue) with the data provider's token
2. Submit the infras
3. Create the contract with the dataset + infras
4. Check roles + cat_item: data-provider approval (provider role + dataset is a DataBank in the DX catalogue, looked up with the provider's token) and infra-provider approval
5. Job status to the user (approved / not approved)
6. gov_layer's signed contract hash goes to the data provider
7. Data provider verifies it, signs with their private key (scripts/contract-sign.sh), sends it back
8. gov_layer verifies the signatures (then the TEE run - endpoint to come).

Fill in: username/password (user), data_provider_username/password, infra_provider_username/password, and data_provider_public_key (from scripts/contract-sign.sh keygen) before step 7a.

item.name: 1. Set the policy for the dataset (data provider's token)

request.description: Data provider's own dev Keycloak token, saved as data_provider_token (used in 1b, 4b, 6, 7a, 7b). Must carry sub/preferred_username and the provider role - if the test fails, paste a token from the dev portal into data_provider_token instead.

exec: console.log('This login returned a token without sub/preferred_username (admin-cli lightweight token) - NOT saved; data_provider_token keeps its current value. Paste a full token from the dev portal into data_provider_token.');
console.log('logged in:', claims.preferred_username || claims.email, '| roles:', roles.join(', '));
pm.test('token names the user (sub + preferred_username or email)', () => pm.expect(claims.sub && (claims.preferred_username || claims.email)).to.be.ok);

item.name: 1b. Set the dataset's policy (as data provider)

request.description: The dataset already exists in the DX catalogue (dataset_id = its catalogue id). This sets the data provider's policy for it in APD, with the data provider's own token; generate-contract (3b) reads the dataset's provider and access rules from this policy. Resending with the same dataset_id updates the policy.
Infra provider's dev Keycloak token, saved as infra_provider_token (used to submit the infras).

exec: console.log('This login returned a token without sub/preferred_username (admin-cli lightweight token) - NOT saved; infra_provider_token keeps its current value. Paste a full token from the dev portal into infra_provider_token.');
console.log('logged in:', claims.preferred_username || claims.email, '| roles:', roles.join(', '));
pm.test('token names the user (sub + preferred_username or email)', () => pm.expect(claims.sub && (claims.preferred_username || claims.email)).to.be.ok);

request.description: Adds infra_id_1 to the infra provider's 'My Infrastructure' in local APD.
Adds infra_id_2 (SMPC needs 2 infra).

item.name: 3. Create the contract with the dataset + infras

request.description: The user who requests the job. Saves access_token; used for 3b (generate contract) and 5 (job status).

Creates the contract with the dataset + infras and its job_id (saved as job_id / contract_id). It is NOT hashed or signed yet: once the job is approved (step 5), gov_layer hashes it, signs the hash with its own private key and sends it to the data provider (step 6 picks up contract_hash).

exec: console.log('job_id', d.contract.job_id, '| approval_required', d.approval_required, '| signing', d.signing);

item.name: 4. Check roles + cat_item, data-provider and infra-provider approval

request.description: Fresh data-provider token (they expire in minutes) for 4b, 6, 7a and 7b.

exec: console.log('This login returned a token without sub/preferred_username (admin-cli lightweight token) - NOT saved; data_provider_token keeps its current value. Paste a full token from the dev portal into data_provider_token.');
console.log('logged in:', claims.preferred_username || claims.email, '| roles:', roles.join(', '));
pm.test('token names the user (sub + preferred_username or email)', () => pm.expect(claims.sub && (claims.preferred_username || claims.email)).to.be.ok);

item.name: 4b. Data-provider approval (provider role + dataset in catalogue)

request.description: Data provider's token (4a). For each of their datasets on the job: the token carries the provider role AND the dataset is an adex:DataBank in the DX catalogue, looked up with that token. 401 missing/invalid token, 403 the token's user provides none of this job's datasets.

exec: console.log('this provider:', d.approval, '| all data providers:', d.data_provider, '| whole job:', d.job_approval, '| sign requests sent:', d.sign_requests_sent);
(d.entries || []).forEach(e => console.log(' ', e.provider_id, e.item, e.status, 'role=' + e.has_role, 'catalogue=' + e.in_catalogue, e.reason || ''));

item.name: 4c. Infra-provider approval (as infra provider: infra-provider role + infras)

request.description: Checks each infra's owner: has the infra-provider role AND the infra is in their APD catalogue. Saved to the audit table. When this (or 4b) makes the whole job approved, the sign requests go out, once.

exec: console.log('this infra provider:', d.approval, '| all infra providers:', d.infra_provider, '| whole job:', d.job_approval, '| sign requests sent:', d.sign_requests_sent);
(d.entries || []).forEach(e => console.log(' ', e.provider_id, e.item, e.status, 'role=' + e.has_role, 'catalogue=' + e.in_catalogue, e.reason || ''));

request.description: The user's own token (3a) - no provider token needed. Data-provider results are the ones the provider recorded in 4b; the infra checks are re-run. Answers only {"status": "approved"} or {"status": "not approved"}; when approved, gov_layer hashes the contract, signs the hash with its private key and sends it to the data provider (step 6). 403 NOT_JOB_CONSUMER for anyone but the contract's user. If the status is not approved, the contract is not hashed, signed or sent, and the collection run stops here.

exec: // Not approved: gov_layer has not hashed, signed or sent the contract - stop here.
console.log('Job not approved - stopping. Fix the rejected check in 4b / 4c and run them again.');

item.name: 6. Governance-signed contract hash sent to the data provider
6. Get the governance-signed hash (as data provider)

exec: const n = reqs.find(n => n.payload.contract_id === cid) || reqs[0];
console.log('contract', n.payload.contract_id, '| hash', n.payload.contract_hash, '| signed by governance:', !!n.payload.governance_signature);

console.log('Now run: scripts/contract-sign.sh sign-request ' + pm.variables.get('data_provider_id') + ' keys/providers/<name>/private.pem ' + pm.variables.get('gov_url') + ' ' + n.payload.contract_id);

item.name: 7. Data provider verifies, signs with their private key, sends back
7a. Register the data provider's public key (once)

request.description:
Once per data provider, before 7b. First, in a terminal (p3dx_gov_layer/):
  scripts/contract-sign.sh keygen keys/providers/<name>
and paste the line it prints into data_provider_public_key. gov_layer verifies the provider's signature against this key; the private key stays on your machine.

item.name: 7b. Send the signed hash back (as data provider)

request.description: Sends the provider's signature (signature variable, from step 6's script) back. The signer is taken from the token. gov_layer re-hashes its copy of the contract, checks its own signature, and verifies the provider's signature against the key from 7a. 409 JOB_NOT_APPROVED if step 5 isn't approved yet. Answers only {"status": "signed", "message": "sent to governance layer"} or {"status": "not signed", "message": <reason>}.

exec: pm.test('signed and sent to governance layer', () => pm.expect(d.status).to.eql('signed'));

item.name: 8. Governance layer verifies the signatures -> TEE

request.description: gov_layer cross-verifies the hash against its copy of the contract, its own signature, and every data provider's signature against their registered key. Answers only {"signatures": "matching", "tee": "can run"} or {"signatures": "not matching", "tee": "cannot run"}.

exec: pm.test('signatures matching - TEE can run', () => pm.expect(d.tee).to.eql('can run'));

item.name: Jobs for a user (GET /jobs/user/{userId})
item.description: Which jobs / contracts each user is participating in, from the governance layer's job_participants table. Run any time after the contract is generated; the statuses move as the job is approved, signed, made final and its TEE enabled.

exec: // consumer's Keycloak user id = the sub claim of their token
console.log('consumer ' + d.user_id + ' is on ' + d.count + ' job(s)');
(d.jobs || []).forEach(j => console.log(j.job_id, j.contract_id, j.technique, j.job_state, JSON.stringify(j.participation.map(p => p.role + ':' + (p.item_id || '-') + ':' + p.status))));

request.description: Every job (contract) the consumer takes part in, newest first: job_id, contract_id, technique, job_state (in_progress / final / tee_enabled) and their participation (role, dataset / infra, status: created / requested / approved / rejected / signed / final / tee_enabled). userId is their Keycloak user id (sub, read from their token above); a username, email or provider id also works.
